blocks.content:
The Prime Minister is the real executive authority.

Appointment:

• Appointed by the President

• Usually leader of majority party in Lok Sabha

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Prime Minister is the real executive authority (de facto executive), whereas the President is the nominal executive authority (de jure executive).
Article 75 mandates that the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
The Prime Minister acts as the principal channel of communication between the President and the Council of Ministers under Article 78.
The Prime Minister serves as the ex-officio Chairman of NITI Aayog, the National Integration Council, and the Inter-State Council.

blocks.content: The Prime Minister is the real executive authority (de facto executive), whereas the President is the nominal executive authority (de jure executive).

items: Powers and Functions of the Prime Minister

blocks.content:
• Head of the Council of Ministers

• Advises the President

• Allocates portfolios

• Leader of Lok Sabha

• Main link between President and Council of Ministers

rows: Leads cabinet meetings and directs policy
Acts on the aid and advice of the Cabinet

blocks.content:
Article 75 provides for a Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President.

Types:

• Cabinet Ministers

• Ministers of State

• Deputy Ministers

Collectively responsible to Lok Sabha.

items: Collective responsibility under Article 75 is specifically to the Lok Sabha, not to Parliament as a whole.
A non-member of Parliament can be appointed as Prime Minister or Minister, but must get elected to either House within six months.
Article 78 defines the explicit duties of the Prime Minister in communicating all decisions of the Council of Ministers to the President.

blocks.content:
• Highest legal officer of the Government of India.

• Appointed by the President.

• Must be qualified to become a Supreme Court judge.

• Has the right to speak in Parliament but cannot vote.
